rationale.conceptual: The paper uses guided-mode resonance and FDTD/RCWA simulation, which are established but non-trivial methods requiring careful implementation of periodic boundary conditions and multi-layer grating stacks. The conceptual challenge lies in correctly translating the physics into simulation parameters and interpreting phase resonance, above textbook operations but not a novel algorithm.
rationale.execution: The reproduction pipeline has only two consecutive steps: run a single electromagnetic simulation to produce reflectance/phase data, then compute a cavity resonance from that data. All I/O is simple CSV, and no external toolchain beyond a standard solver library (e.g., S4, Meep) is required. No multi-stage dependencies, data fetching, or fragile orchestration.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires simulating a cross-stacked grating with an electromagnetic solver (FDTD/RCWA) to extract reflectance and phase, then solving a Fabry-Perot resonance condition. The method is an established computational electromagnetics technique applied to a specific geometry; setting up the solver correctly for a two-layer orthogonal grating structure demands some domain knowledge but is not algorithmically novel. The pipeline has two straightforward steps with no heavy orchestration or data dependencies, running on a CPU with modest resources.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The simulation domain is a few micrometers with thin layers; the EM solver (RCWA or FDTD) runs on CPU with moderate memory. No large external datasets are needed—only inline material parameters.
